name: はし田屋 本店 (Hashidaya Honten)

claims.text: The oyakodon sauce and yakitori tare are traditional soy-sauce (shoyu) based preparations; no wheat-free or gluten-free soy sauce alternative was found advertised.

Eel is prepared to order (butterflied, steamed, then charcoal-grilled after the order is placed) rather than held pre-cooked, and the cooking method is grilling rather than deep-frying, so there is no shared tempura fryer in the process.

name: レストラン はやしや (Hayashiya (Restaurant Hayashiya))

claims.text: Menu is centered on wheat-flour-based demi-glace sauces and panko-breaded cutlets; no wheat-free soy sauce or GF sauce alternative was mentioned in any source.

name: 秀吉 神保町水道橋店 (Hideyoshi Jimbocho Suidobashi-ten)

claims.text: Kushi-katsu and karaage are deep-fried items on the menu alongside grilled skewers; no separate/dedicated fryer for allergen-free items was mentioned in any source.

The restaurant's own original sauce and yakitori tare are described as blended seasoning sauces typical of this izakaya style, which in Japan are standardly soy-sauce (wheat-containing) based; no wheat-free tare or shoyu was mentioned.

name: 火鍋 小肥羊 新宿西口店 (Hinabe Xiaofeiyang Shinjuku Nishiguchi-ten)

claims.text: The white and spicy mala hot pot broths are made with chicken extract, beef extract, and bonito (fish) extract as their base, so the broth itself is not vegan or vegetarian even when only vegetables and tofu are added to it.

name: ひない小町 渋谷店 (Hinai Komachi Shibuya)

claims.text: Standard yakitori tare glaze is soy-sauce based (contains wheat); no confirmation found of a wheat-free tare or dedicated GF sauce.
Shio (salt-grilled, no soy-based tare) yakitori is a standard menu option alongside tare-glazed skewers, which may reduce wheat exposure if confirmed with staff.

name: いろり庵きらく そば 水道橋店 (Iroriann Kiraku Soba - Suidobashi Branch)

claims.text: Udon and Chinese-style (wheat) noodles are boiled in the same pot as the soba noodles, so those with wheat allergy or celiac disease need to be careful even with a plain soba order.

The tsuyu, which contains soy sauce, is prepared in a shared kitchen alongside items containing wheat, soy, and mackerel; the chain's allergen chart notes that allergens not listed as direct ingredients can still be introduced via shared equipment/facilities.
The chain (excluding a couple of named branches) publishes a company-wide allergen chart covering its menu and directs customers with concerns to check it or ask staff.

name: 海鮮と炉端焼き 囲炉裏 新宿 (Kaisen to Robatayaki Irori Shinjuku (Seafood)

claims.text: No wheat-free/gluten-free soy sauce alternative is advertised on any listing; as a standard robatayaki/oden izakaya, regular (wheat-containing) shoyu should be assumed throughout the menu.
